Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Aindrī, Vārāhī, and likewise Vaiṣṇavī; Rudrakālī, Viśālākṣī, Bhairavī, and Kālarūpiṇī. || 22-155 ||
Mahāmāyā, of great enthusiasm, the great destroyer of the fierce;
the glory of the Kula, filled with the Kula, dwelling within the womb of the Kula. || 22-156 ||
She is the charcoal of the lineage, endowed with the lineage, joined with the tresses of the lineage;
she is the one who grasps the *darbha* grass of the lineage and the bestower of the pit of the lineage. || 22-157 ||
Endowed with love for her family, virtuous, devoted to Śiva, offering oblations to Śiva, attached to Śiva, having Śiva as her very life-breath, she made Mahādeva her abode. (22.158)

The beloved consort of Mahādeva, she who is intoxicated with love for Mahādeva; the nourisher of the passion of both the intoxicated and the non-intoxicated, she who increases prosperity. || 22-159 ||
Intoxicated with passion, supremely pure, adorned with the intoxication of love, her face radiant with exhilaration, she is intent upon intoxicated kisses. || 22-160 ||
Damayantī was intent on intoxicated play, and her mind was like that of a daughter of the Himavat;
she was overcome by passion, moved by intoxication, and devoted to inverted love-making.
Bestower of wealth, delighting in wealth, and intent upon the increase of wealth—thus has this entire thousand names of Kālī been recounted to you. (1100) [22.162]
This divine [mantra] is the most essential of the essential, increasing great prosperity;
it bestows the status of a leader of the Gaṇas, grants sovereignty, and accomplishes the six rites.
The practitioner who recites this constantly shall become the abode of all accomplishments;
whoever recites it, causes it to be recited, hears it, or causes it to be heard—[shall likewise attain success]. (22.164)
By the grace of this hymn, nothing whatsoever is difficult to obtain in this world—not even the killing of a Brahmin, the drinking of liquor, or likewise the theft of gold. (22.165)
Approaching the wife of one's guru and whatever other evil deed has been committed—all this it purifies; this is the truth, O you who are worshipped by the hosts of gods. (22.166)
Upon seeing a woman in her menses, one should recite this hymn with undistracted mind;
he shall indeed become Śiva and a speaker of truth—of this there is no doubt. (22.167)
Having united with another's wife, if one recites this hymn with a concentrated mind, one shall become endowed with all sovereign powers and attain the status of a great king. || 22-168 ||
One should not cause slander of others, malice toward others, or injury to others, even toward one who is a devotee of Śiva, one who is peaceful, or one who is fond of devotion. (22.169)
And one should show this hymn to him; otherwise, he would meet his death.
O Goddess of the Gods, there is nothing superior to this within the Tantra.
Mahākālī, Mahādevī, and likewise Nīlasarasvatī—there is no difference between them, O Supreme Goddess; he who creates such a distinction shall go to hell.
This divine hymn is proclaimed by me out of affection for you;
thus, there is oneness between both, and one should not resort to the notion of duality.
O Supreme Goddess, such a yogi is equal in honor and dishonor.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Thousand Names of Kālī," in the dialogue between Bhairava and Pārvatī within the illustrious Bṛhannīlatantra. || 22 ||
Now begins the twenty-third chapter.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, long ago you made a promise when you were intent on play:
"O Master, tell the hundred names of Mahākālī to me. (23-1)
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"Well asked, O Great Goddess! I shall tell you that which is not to be told.
It must not be disclosed, O beautiful one, dear to the best of men, for it is like one's own womb."
O enchantress, you are dearer to me than my own life;
O Supreme Goddess, I cannot live for even a single moment without you. (23-3)
Just as a reflection of ghee, curd, and other substances appears in a stainless mirror,
so do I, O Primordial One, become perceptible everywhere within you, who are the source of all worlds.
Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare that which bestows omniscience through recitation;
Sadāśiva is said to be the seer (ṛṣi), and Anuṣṭubh is declared to be the meter (chandas). (23–5)
O Goddess, Bhairava is the deity for the four aims of human life;
his application (viniyoga) should be employed as the bestower of the fruits of all actions. (23-6)

Mahākālī, the sustainer of the world, the mother of the world, whose essence is the world; the Mother of the World, whose strength is ever-manifesting, she who brings joy to the world. (10) || 23-7 ||
Gaurī, the destroyer of the world, the dispeller of suffering and poverty,
the mother of Bhairava, the infinite in being, and the bestower of eloquence.

The virtuous one who bestows the four aims of life, the auspiciousness of all auspicious things, Bhadrakālī (20), the large-eyed one, the granter of desires, whose essence is the artistic arts. (23.9)
Blue-voiced, with all her limbs exceedingly fair, she is the supreme beauty;
she bestows all prosperity, roars with a formidable sound, and possesses an excellent complexion.
She of the excellent gait (30), she whose feet are auspicious, the slayer of the demon Mahiṣāsura;
she who is worshipped by Śiva, beloved of Śiva, and honored by the lords of the Dānavas. || 23-11 ||
She consists of all knowledge, she bestows all desired fruits upon everyone;
she has delicate limbs, she is the creator, and she grants boons to the Creator. (40) || 23-12 ||
With a face like the full moon, the color of a dark cloud, bearing a skull-cup, Kurukullā is of noble mind, delights the heart of her beloved, and is intoxicated with passion. (23.13)
She has limbs intoxicated with passion, she delights in love, her eyes roll with intoxication;
she has emerged from the wine-vat and sports with skulls and human heads held in her hands. (50) 23.14.
The Goddess, garlanded with human skulls, holding a sword in her hand, is terrifying;
she is endowed with a boisterous laugh, is lotus-like, and is adorned with rubies. (23.15)
Bestower of boons and fearlessness (60), Kālī, whose nature is that of Kālarātri;
she is Svadhā, Svāhā, and Vaṣaṭkāra, possessing a radiance equal to the autumnal moon. || 23-16 ||
She is like the autumn moonlight, bringing great delight; she is distressed by inverted sexual union;
she has loose hair, severed matted locks, and sports with a mass of matted hair.
Terrifying, joined with the King of Serpents, she stands upon the King of Serpents;
dwelling in the cremation ground, she is praised by Mahānandi, her eyes blazing with light. (23.18)
Delighting in the corpse-seat, she is Nandā, served by Siddhas and Cāraṇas;
she is fond of offerings of bali, she is the womb, and she is the embodiment of the worlds Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ. (23.19)
Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Mahānīlasarasvatī, and Lakṣmī, endowed with auspicious marks and characterized by all the signs of excellence. || 23-20 ||
Clad in a tiger skin (90), pure, and adorned with three folds, she is indeed praised by the Gandharvas and likewise by the great Indra; she is the supreme goddess. 23-21.
The supreme purifier, the great illusion, the great source of prosperity—(100) thus, O Great Goddess, have these one hundred divine names been told to you. (23-22)
Whoever recites this upon rising in the morning shall become a treasury of knowledge;
having enjoyed happiness in this world, he shall attain union with the Goddess. || 23-23 ||

These streams of perfected beings, including all that is mobile and immobile— those who move through the sky, those who move upon the earth, and likewise those who move in heaven— become subject to his will.
All of them indeed come under the control of the practitioner; it is not otherwise, O Maheśānī, even if one were to abandon this excellent thousand names. (23–25)
O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, O Supreme Sovereign, one should recite this hundred [names] which bestows the fruits of the four aims of life;
for without knowing these hundred names, O Great Goddess, [the goal cannot be attained]. (23–26)
For one who worships Mahākālī, there is no lack of accomplishment in the Kali Yuga;
listen now to the meritorious fruit for him who recites this with devotion and self-restraint. (23–27)
The fruit of worshipping Kālī for a hundred thousand years shall be attained.
What is the use of saying more here? One will obtain whatever object is desired. (23–28)
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Hundred Names of Kālī," in the dialogue between Bhairava and Pārvatī within the illustrious Bṛhannīlatantra.
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter.
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, Great God, cause of creation, preservation, and destruction!
Speak with a concentrated mind that which was declared in the *Annadākalpa*. (24.1)
"I shall tell you the supreme and specific mantra for the giver of food;
O auspicious one, as this was told to me, relate it with a concentrated mind. (24.2)
Śrī Bhairava said: O Śivā, O Supreme Goddess, as it is with Kālī, so it is with Nīlā and likewise with Annadā;
their mantra has been declared in this [context].
O beautiful one, I have described to you the supreme kalpa of Annadā, she who, as a single form, becomes threefold for the benefit of the worlds. 24-4.

O Great Goddess, O Beloved, listen with one-pointed mind to the King of Mantras: "O Great Goddess, [the syllable] *anna* as a phoneme, endowed with the sound *mahikāra*; and likewise the phoneme *anna*, adorned at its beginning by a vowel. O Goddess, [the syllable] *anādhi* as red, joined with the word *taye*. My food (*mama annam*)..."
"O Īśānī, grant me a place; then, [grant] a place"—this is the mantra mentioned in another Tantra.
[One should employ] a mount for the journey that has ceased yawning and has abandoned its side. 24-5.
O Goddess, joined with the left eye and endowed with the bindu, this is the supreme first seed-syllable, O Parameśvarī; thus it has been declared. (24.6)
And then, O Goddess, there is the syllable *lohitam* (blood), adorned with the first vowel;
it has the color of food, O Great Goddess, and is joined with the letters *ma* and *e*. (24.7)
O Great Goddess, it is not of many colors, but adorned with the first vowel; and then, O Supreme Mistress, there is the three-worded secret of all. (24.8)
O Great Goddess, this mantra is secret and ends with the wife of Fire (svāhā).
O Great Goddess, this mantra bestows accomplishment through sheer force.
All matters such as meditation and worship have been explained in the previous chapter;
now I shall proclaim the hundred names that bestow all eloquence.
Without that [mantra], even if a man worships Mahādevī for a hundred thousand years, his success does not arise. (24.11)
Therefore, with every effort, listen attentively;
O beautiful one, this supreme thousand names has been told to you.
Now listen, O Goddess of gods, to the one named Annadāśata;
there is nothing superior to this within the tantras, O Maheśvarī. (24.13)
The giver of food, the supreme Māyā, the Great Goddess beloved of Śiva;
Bhavānī, the primordial source of the worlds, the giver of life, dearer than life itself. (24.14)
She consists of the life-force of the world (10), she is Gaurī, she is the supreme Trayī consisting of the Vedas;
she dwells in the city of Kāśī and she is the destroyer of the city of Kāśī. || 24-15 ||
Kālī, whose abode is Kailāsa, who knows the cosmic cycles and bestows them, she is auspicious;
she is worshipped by Mahādeva and is intensely devoted to Mahādeva. (24.16)
The goddess is fond of milk-rice, possesses full and elevated breasts,
is endowed with the three folds of skin on her waist, and has the most excellent and beautiful eyes.
Holding an infinite alms-bowl, she is intent upon seeking food;
she is the Gaṅgā, the Gayā, the large-eyed one, and possesses a vast form and youth. (24.18)
Intoxicated with passion, her own form as her body, her face resembling the full moon, her life-breath is Śiva, she delights in Śiva, and she is the great cloud of Sadāśiva. (24.19)
She is the beloved of Mahādeva, the virtuous Satī, languid with passion, and dear to her husband;
she has delicate limbs, is skilled in the arts of love, the very limit of beauty, and renowned for her glory. (24.20)
She whose face is like a full-blown lotus, who has a lotus as her abode, who is auspicious, Bhavānī, who delights in her home, and who rests upon a lotus seat. (24.21)
Surrounded by Siddhas and Gandharvas and likewise praised by the Rishis, she sat together with Shiva, intent upon the divine play of Shiva. (60) 24.22
A young woman, delighted by youth and ever intent on perpetual youth, she was always sixteen years of age and enchanting to Sadāśiva. (24.23)
She possessed a beautiful form, a lovely face, and graceful prowess;
her limbs were exquisite, her body was golden, and she stood upon gold.
Aṇṇapūrṇā is ever-full, adorned with golden bracelets;
she is the life-breath of her devotees, devoted to her devotees, and intent on feeding her devotees. || 24-25 ||
She who loves clarified butter (ājyapriyā), the many-eyed one (virūpākṣī), the auspicious wearer of a crow’s wing (kākapakṣadharā);
she who bestows auspiciousness, the beautiful, the pure, the partless, the supreme goal. (24–26)
She is fond of the distressed, devoted to the distressed, and intent on providing food for the distressed;
she is endowed with love for the practitioner and bestows fearlessness upon the practitioner.
She dwells together with the practitioners, gratified by the love of the practitioners;
she is the bestower of bliss to the practitioners and the object of the practitioners' love. (24–28)
The sustainer of the world, the protector of the world, the bringer of victory to the worlds—(100) thus has this auspicious, divine hundred names of Annapūrṇā been told to you. (24–29)
Whoever recites this upon rising in the morning shall become the Supreme Lord;
and even a poor person, O Goddess, shall obtain every kind of prosperity.
O fair-browed one! He becomes free from disease and becomes a knower of the meaning of all scriptures;
O Sovereign of the Gods, no anxiety regarding food shall arise in his lineage. (24–31)
O Supreme Goddess, he shall become a lord victorious over the three worlds;
even a barren woman obtains a son, and a maiden finds a virtuous husband. (24.32)
By reciting or even by memorizing it, a person becomes identical with all [deities].
This hymn, more secret than the secret, is concealed within all tantras. (24–33)
Out of affection for you, O lady of excellent limbs, this has been revealed before you.
It must not be disclosed, O Great Goddess; it must never be disclosed.
O Maheśānī, reveal it to my devotee;
Vyāsa and others, as well as Vasiṣṭha and all his followers, are its worshippers.
O Goddess of gods, Ekānnapūrṇā appears in manifold ways through her various forms:
as Kālī, Tārā, Mahāvidyā, and the Supreme Sovereign Annadā. (24–36)
O Great Goddess, these are the sciences that are perfected in the Kali age;
O Supreme Sovereign, they are attained through the good fortune of many births. (24–37)
O lady of excellent limbs, listen to the fruit of merit for those who, by the power of fortune alone, become true worshippers of these [goddesses]. (24–38)
He becomes a poet, wise, and the best of practitioners; by the mere grasping of this mantra, a human being becomes perfected. (24-39)
O Goddess, having received this mantra for the sake of dharma, pleasure, wealth, and liberation, practitioners free from envy considered nothing to be unattainable. (24.40)
O Great Goddess, he who worships these daily with a spirit of devotion will become like Kubera in his sovereignty. (24.41)
Indeed, all eight perfections (siddhis) become mines of knowledge for him alone;
O Supreme Goddess, merely by seeing his abundance of wealth, [others are moved]. (24.42)
Even Indra, O Supreme Goddess, seems like another inferior being;
blessed is his mother, and his father is the best of gods. (24.43)
He who knows these [mantras] in their true essence from the mouth of one who knows the tradition shall, by the mere knowledge of them, deliver ten million members of his lineage. (24.44)
All the ancestors rejoice and sing this verse with joy:
"Will there be someone in our lineage who possesses knowledge of the family? (24.45)
One should desire many sons, even if only one should remain to uphold the lineage;
for what is the use of offering funeral cakes at Gayā, and what is the use of traveling to Kāśī? (24.46)
O Śivā, if by the power of fortune alone one worships the Great Goddess Kālī, Sarasvatī, and Annapūrṇā in the courtyard of the house, [one attains success].
He is a brahmin, he is a knower of the Vedas, he is self-controlled, and he is an adept;
he is a dweller at sacred fords among the seats, like one belonging to the fourth stage of life.
He shall become a renunciant, a great yogi, and liberated while living;
O Great Goddess, O fair-faced one, for him there is neither sin nor merit. (24.49)
O woman of excellent complexion, there is no fault whatsoever arising from acts such as violence, even if there were a woman equal to you and a man equal to me. (24.50)
At that time, there is indeed no mantra equal to these perfected vidyās;
having abandoned the mantras of others, one should take refuge in this mantra. (24.51)
Among the three crores [of scriptures], the essence of the Tantras has been revealed;
O Supreme Goddess, that which has been spoken must be performed day and night. (24–52)
O Great Goddess, O Beloved, in whatever house this tantra resides, my own presence certainly dwells there, O Great Goddess. (24-53)
He certainly becomes possessed of all branches of knowledge; there is no doubt whatsoever.
Sovereignty and freedom from disease shall always abide in his home. (24.54)
I am Śiva and the Supreme Self, while Maheśvarī is my mother.
O Maheśānī, O Śivā, everything that is difficult to obtain has now been told.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the illustrious *Bṛhannīlatantra*, the most excellent among all excellent tantras, in the dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī, titled "The Determination of the Greatness of the Tantra and the Extraction of the Mantra of Annadā along with its Hundred Names."
And thus concludes this Śrī Bṛhannīlatantra. In the Vikrama year measured by five, nine, and the moon (1995),
[this] Śrī Nīlatantra, the essence of all remaining Tantras, [is completed].
Having refined this highly precious jewel from the great ocean of the Śrī Bhairavāgama by means of textual emendations, the restoration of pure readings, and other such methods; || 1 ||
Having diligently recovered even ancient manuscripts written by the hands of former scribes that had long been worn out,
[I shall compose this work] whose splendor flashes with the qualities of magnanimity, heroism, and beauty.
By the command of King Harisiṃha, the king of kings.
In this work concerning the office of the learned Śrī Rāmacandra— who belongs to the lineage of Kāka and holds a high position—
Śāstrī, having received the assistance of Śivanātha, has brought it to completion.
This was revealed by the scholar Śāstrī Harabhaṭṭa Vipañcit. || 3 ||
